runConfig.positivePrompt: Scientific educational image-to-video for ages five to fourteen. Static locked wide camera, one continuous five-second shot with no cuts, no reversed footage, and no repeated segment. Preserve the attached approved still as the exact first-frame Ankylosaurus magniventris identity, low broad full-body anatomy, left-facing composition, wetland, lighting, palette, armor pattern, ground, and crop reference. Exactly one complete Ankylosaurus remains with one broad flat skull, small beaked mouth, two neck half-rings, irregular low osteoderms, exactly four planted legs, one continuous tail, and one integrated low oval tail club. The dinosaur itself performs one continuous natural feeding sequence: the complete head and connected neck move forward and down by a controlled visible distance, the small beak opens slightly and closes once on the nearest fern tips, the lower jaw makes one slow chew, and the throat contracts once. The head then remains in the final low feeding pose without returning to the first pose. Only the touched fern tips may bend slightly at the mouth; all other background pixels remain still. Keep the torso, pelvis, armor rows, four feet, toes, full tail, and club stable. No reverse playback, repeated bite, head bob loop, step, body turn, or tail movement.
